heading: What each realm refuses
body:
Every annotation above appears in each language that accepts it. The missing examples are not mistakes. The compiler rejects these combinations before anything runs, and its error message says why.

A native Tac service is written in Swift, Kotlin, C# or Rust, and it is a plain type. It accepts Service, Lifetime and NeedsAll, the data and behavior annotations, Setup, Needs, Named, CacheSettings, Entity, Table, Store, Checked, Settings, WhenProfile and WhenSetting. It refuses the annotations that depend on a browser container. Helper and the browser resources fail with TY1308. StreamRequest and SocketRequest clients are written in JavaScript or TypeScript only. A client in any other Tac language fails with TY1308 at the client file, and the message names its language, for example `@StreamRequest is not available in Java Tac code`, or `[<SocketRequest>] is not available in F# Tac code` in F#. HTTPClient fails with a message that gives the reason. Its transport, which the framework manages, belongs to the browser (ADR 0027). Instead, a native service reaches the network through HTTP request annotations and an adapter that you configure yourself.

InBackground listeners (methods that run when an event happens) need a language whose methods can be asynchronous. In Yon, these languages are JavaScript, TypeScript and Python. PHP, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, F#, Rust, Dart, Go, Ruby and Lua reject the annotation. They do not pretend to delay the call.

Stream needs the language's own generator syntax (a way to return values one at a time). JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Kotlin, C#, F#, Dart and Ruby have it, Lua sends each value with `coroutine.yield`, and Go returns an `iter.Seq` (Go's range-over-function iterator). Java, Groovy and Rust stay single-response. They return the whole collection at once.

Topic is refused, with TY1308, on a Lua model in both realms and on a Python model in Tac. Those languages get topics in a later step, so publish or listen in another language of the same realm.

Both realms refuse a field that Tachyon fills, a Needs field or a NeedsAll field without a starting value, when it is declared nullable. Tachyon never leaves such a field null, so `label?: string` or `final String? path;` would only mislead the reader. The build stops with TY1331 and shows the non-null form to write instead. Both realms also refuse, with TY1332, a field that holds an injected class and does not use the language's variable case, such as `CartStore CartStore;` in Java or `cartStore` in Python.

Gateway exists only in Yon. A Tac service has no supervisor that could start another language for one call. So the annotation fails with TY1308 in every Tac language. Public, SignedIn, Allow and IdentityProvider exist only in Yon, because only a server can decide who may call a route. A Tac page cannot protect data: the server route must say who may call it.
